newsitem.title: USA: Lilly says Guardsman acquisition boosts Q4.
newsitem.headline: Lilly says Guardsman acquisition boosts Q4.

text.p: Lilly Industries Inc said Monday its higher fiscal 1996 fourth quarter results reflected contributions from Guardsman Products Inc which was acquired in April 1996.

Lilly reported its sales for its fiscal fourth quarter ended November 30, 1996 rose 85 percent to a record $153.1 million from $82.8 million for the same quarter a year earlier. Earnings rose to a record $7.7 million, 46 percent above the $5.2 million in the 1995 fourth quarter. Per share earnings rose to $0.33 from $0.23 last year.

For its fiscal 1996 year, sales increased 55 percent from a year ago to $509 million. Net income declined to $18.8 million or $0.81 from $20.3 million or $0.88 a year earlier due to a one-time $9.6 million restructuring charge taken in the second quarter from integrating Guardsman.
Lilly said cost savings from combining the companies in 1996 totaled $17 million and an additional $8 million in costs is expected to be saved in 1997.

Lilly said that higher sales, increased gross profit, and cost reductions resulted in a $10.1 million increase in operating income. Increased operating income more than offset the additional interest expense which Lilly incurred from the acquisition of Guardsman.

Looking ahead, Lilly Chairman and President Douglas Huemme said, "Management is optimistic for 1997. Restructuring charges are behind us and operating costs are declining due to elimination of redundant functions; manufacturing efficiencies are improving; and our business outlook is solid," he said.
Lilly makes industrial coatings and specialty chemical products. Its shares were trading up 1/4 at 19-1/8.
